topic: Making room for grief at Christmas (carousel)
caption:
How to make room for grief at Christmas, for yourself and the people you love.

The holidays are built from memory, so the absence of someone we love can feel sharpest now. Researchers who studied widowed older adults suggest that a chance to talk about memories of the person, or a private celebration of the day, may help some people. There is no right way to do this season.

New blog up now. Link in bio.

Share with someone who might find this helpful.

Research:
Carr, D., Sonnega, J., Nesse, R. M., & House, J. S. (2014). Do special occasions trigger psychological distress among older bereaved spouses? An empirical assessment of clinical wisdom. The Journals of Gerontology: Series B, 69(1), 113-122. https://doi.org/10.1093/geronb/gbt061

This content is for general informational purposes and does not constitute psychological advice. Grief can be very personal. If you are experiencing significant distress, please speak with a registered health professional, or call Lifeline on 13 11 14.
